page: Microsoft Azure E32-8as_v5 is a constrained vCPU memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with x86_64 architecture, providing 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores clocked at 3.525 GHz. The CPU features 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside support for AES, AVX, and BMI2 instruction extensions. The instance is provisioned with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 32.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated hardware accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded CPU capability, with stress-ng single-core throughput placing in the top 25% of evaluated cloud systems at 2739.08. Multi-core compute performance remains moderate, posting a Geekbench multi-core score of 6328.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 10807.84. Memory subsystem benchmarks show high cached read bandwidth at 515.82 GB/sec, though uncached large-block write operations register lower relative throughput at 22.68 GB/sec. In-memory data store evaluations demonstrate reliable throughput, achieving 8.24 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads alongside static web throughput of 10.21 GB/sec.

From an architectural standpoint, the constrained 8-vCPU configuration paired with a full 256.0 GB memory footprint offers significant software licensing efficiency. Workloads licensed per core that require high memory allocations avoid paying for unneeded compute cycles. However, the absence of local ephemeral storage necessitates remote Azure Premium Storage attachments, which can introduce latency boundaries for write-heavy pipelines. The E32-8as_v5 is best configured for memory-intensive relational databases, large in-memory caches, enterprise ERP deployments, and analytics workloads requiring massive memory spaces with moderate parallel processing demands.
